pairs.evidence: packages/catalog/src/partOptions.ts:3 The catalog in this context holds creative content (presets, recipes, styles, projects, deck art, library areas) plus PART_OPTIONS, a code-constant table of model options by work kind. None of it is a registry of external integration types: there is no auth schema, no credential form, no probe recipe, no operator-writable store and no foreign-name resolver. A search of packages/catalog and packages/ui for authSchema, auth_schema, apiKey, api_key and connectorId found 0 files. The only 'connector' and 'credential' hits in packages/ui/src are a bracket line connector and an identity-refresh comment.

techniques.evidence: packages/catalog/src/partOptions.ts:111 Rows are data keyed by a provider string, but they describe model options (lane, pace, usage units) per work kind, not integration types with identity, auth, probe and taxonomy. This is closer to model-routing/cost-metering.
packages/catalog/src/projects.ts:2 Catalog entries are compiled constants. No refresh writes shipped rows into an operator-editable store, so there is no two-writer table.
packages/catalog/src/partOptions.ts:57 The only vendor-specific declaration is a voice id. No row declares credential fields or a probe, so there is no form or vacuous-green question.
packages/catalog/src/partOptions.ts:76 Lookup is an exact internal key match. No foreign vocabulary is resolved to catalog identity, so tiers and no-match guards do not arise.
packages/catalog/src/partOptions.ts:8 Provider translation (producers, router) lives outside this context, in packages/kernel and lib/producers. This context holds no adapter code.

packages/catalog/src/partOptions.ts:64 The nearest lifecycle fact is a dated vendor-voice expiry kept in a comment. With no installed rows and no dependent credential instances, there are no tombstones and no set difference to compute.
